US stock earnings outlook weakens｜ETH price around $2666｜I’m watching risk appetite first

My stance is cautious, but I won’t take sell-side earnings forecasts for US stocks as a direct instruction for ETH’s rise and fall. On Binance Square, the #WallStreetEarningsRevisionsTurnBearish headline refers to changes in equity analysts’ earnings expectations. In a Sept. 23 report, Bloomberg cited a Citi US Earnings Revisions Index: the number of analysts lowering forecasts first exceeded those raising forecasts in over 23 weeks. This is the Citi indicator quoted in the report—it is not earnings that companies have already reported as declining, nor is it Ethereum on-chain revenue data. Earlier, on Sept. 4, FactSet noted that S&P 500 constituents’ quarterly EPS estimates had been revised up for the second consecutive quarter. The two observations use different dates and methodologies; you can’t erase one, and you also can’t write “revisions turning negative” as if all companies’ earnings are collapsing.

Why should ETH traders care? If equity earnings expectations weaken and stay weak, traditional risk-asset valuation tolerance may drop, and the same pool of capital may reduce positions in high-volatility crypto assets. But this is a cross-market risk-appetite transmission hypothesis—not proven causality. ETH still has its own drivers: stablecoin usage and DeFi activity, staking and fund subscription/redemption, and protocol progress. These factors could offset or amplify macro pressure. If you tag ETH as “must fall” based only on hot-topic headlines, you ignore timing and capital differences on both sides.

When I checked KuCoin’s ETH/USDT spot, it was about $2666.05, down about 1.78% over the past 24 hours. The range was a high of $2723.44 and a low of $2628.58. The current price hasn’t reclaimed 2700, suggesting risk appetite has not yet given a clear repair signal through price action. However, this drop occurred within a 24-hour window, so it can’t be attributed to one Citi index reading. 2700 is the integer level I watch for a sentiment recovery signal; around 2723 is the high for this leg; and around 2629 is the low that has already formed. If price later holds steadily above 2700 with spot follow-through, my cautious judgment would be invalidated. If it breaks below 2629 again, I’ll first concede that the market is weaker in the short term.

If I were trading for myself, I wouldn’t participate. I would only consider a spot long after conditions are met, and I wouldn’t place high-leverage short positions. Only if two consecutive full 15-minute candlesticks close above 2700, and a pullback to 2685—2700 holds without breaking, while the broader market’s risk appetite does not continue to deteriorate, would I use no more than 0.3% of total capital for the trial order. First target: trim half around 2723. Second target: close the remaining position around 2750. After entry, if the first 15-minute candle pulls back below 2675, I cut the position in half immediately. If it loses 2650, I stop out everything right away and close. If 2629 breaks before entry, this long plan is void. If, two hours after entering, price still can’t push toward 2723, I would also close proactively. If the conditions aren’t triggered, there’s no trade—so I won’t write this “observation” as profit.

The DCAP ETF just launched and immediately turned things up—splitting investors’ money into two halves: one half into the Strategy preferred shares (high dividend + volatility risk), and the other into the Strive preferred shares (low dividend + exposure linked to crypto assets). This bold allocation has drawn plenty of investors who want to “bet on returns” but are afraid it might be too wild. Still, when dividend sources are assets like Bitcoin—which can swing dramatically—can the risk really be kept under control? For BTC/ETH holders looking to buy via ETFs, it may mean more than they think—maybe even less.

Why this news matters
The DCAP ETF’s model is significant because it directly addresses two major pain points in the crypto market: how to earn stable returns amid high volatility, and how to let traditional capital in—and keep it there. Most ETFs today mainly profit by betting on Bitcoin’s price movement. DCAP’s split model, in essence, is playing a “dividend game.” If BTC can truly keep paying dividends, it would be a major positive for the overall valuation of crypto assets. But if BTC can’t even protect its own costs, dividends become empty promises. The success of this setup hinges on whether crypto assets can become “high-quality, consistently paying” assets.

Market impact
- On BTC/ETH prices: In the short term, it may boost sentiment for crypto equities, since ETF innovation often comes with bullish speculation. But the long-term test is whether BTC can actually deliver stable dividends like a mature industry. If BTC keeps surging, dividend pressure will be huge. If BTC crashes, dividends likely can’t even be paid. That means BTC needs to stay above $85K for the DCAP model to look like a can’t-lose business.
- On market structure: These ETFs could accelerate segmentation in the crypto market—some people bet on asset price increases, others bet on dividends. This supply-demand mismatch could feed through to BTC/ETH prices. Simply put: capital is no longer one solid block; it now has more “allocation choices.” That could be a positive for the absolute upside of BTC/ETH, but a potential negative for how fast the upside comes.

Trading/investment approach
💡 Personal view: This DCAP model is a trial run of a “crypto dividend revolution.” If BTC can maintain stable dividend payouts above $80K, it would greatly increase market appeal. But the failure condition is clear: once BTC falls below $78K, the valuation of the Strive preferred shares tied to crypto assets would be cut in half, and the entire ETF’s appeal would collapse instantly. To me, that means the upside potential of this type of ETF is limited unless BTC holds steady above $80K.

Recently, a long-dated Bitcoin options trade has been finalized—this deal won’t expire until 2028. The news frames it as a sign that institutions are growing more confident in the digital-asset market and that the market is becoming more mature. What does that mean? In short, some institutions are willing to play these long-term “bets” through options, not just chase small, near-term gains. It suggests they believe Bitcoin can be around for a long time.

Why is this news important?
The core reason is that, in the past, institutions didn’t dare to touch Bitcoin—an inherently high-risk asset. Now they’re willing to accept long-term risk exposure. Why? The Bitcoin market is slowly taking shape: exchanges are starting to offer options, regulation is gradually loosening, and institutions finally have legal channels to participate. This is similar to the recent approval of spot Bitcoin ETFs—both point to a market that’s improving.

What does it mean for the market?
First, market participants won’t focus solely on short-term volatility; they’re willing to back long-horizon bets. Second, long-dated options can help institutions hedge risk—for example, buying a long-dated put option to protect against Bitcoin falling too much. This makes market tools more diverse.

Market impact
For BTC and ETH prices, the short term may get a sentiment boost, since institutional involvement is typically viewed positively. But the long-term trend still depends on Bitcoin’s own performance—mining costs, and whether new applications can truly emerge. In terms of market structure, it shows Bitcoin transitioning from pure speculation toward a real financial asset. Regarding the regulatory environment, if long-dated options trading develops, it may pressure regulators to provide even more support. On capital flows, you may see more traditional funds moving into the Bitcoin market.

这件事根本原因在于，以前机构不敢玩比特币这种高风险资产，现在他们愿意接受长期的风险敞口。为啥？因为比特币市场慢慢有样了——交易所开始做期权，监管也在慢慢松绑，机构有地方合法地参与进来。这跟最近比特币现货ETF获批有点像，都是说市场在变好。

对市场来说，这意味着啥？首先，市场参与者不再只盯着短期波动，愿意为长期赌局买单。其次，这种长期期权交易能帮机构对冲风险，比如买一个长期看跌期权来防着比特币跌太多。这会让市场工具更丰富。

对市场的影响
对BTC和ETH价格，短期可能是个情绪提振，毕竟机构入场总是好事。但长期趋势还得看比特币自己表现，比如挖矿成本、新应用能不能出来。对市场格局，说明比特币从纯投机品开始向真正的金融资产过渡。对监管环境，这种长期期权交易如果发展起来，可能会倒逼监管给更多支持。资金流向上，可能会看到更多传统资金往比特币市场里流。

历史参考有点少，因为长期比特币期权交易还是个新鲜事。但可以想想黄金ETF怎么发展的，也是从没人玩到慢慢机构接受。

📰 Could EU energy weapons smash encrypted locks? Quantum computers threaten BTC/ETH

EU regulators have issued a warning: quantum computing technology may break blockchain encryption within the next few years, posing potential risks to Bitcoin and to Ethereum—targeting full deflation by 2029—that are considering technological migration. This isn’t alarmism—today’s quantum computers can already crack the RSA-2048 encryption algorithm within minutes, and both Bitcoin and Ethereum rely on similar cryptographic foundations.

Why is this news important?
Quantum computing is not a sci-fi concept. There are already quantum computers with 53 qubits in development, and they are expected to reach the capability to break elliptic-curve cryptography within 5–10 years. That means Bitcoin private keys and Ethereum account balances could face a risk of being "brute-forced." This threat is critical because it exposes an "Achilles' heel" in the blockchain’s underlying logic: all major public chains are based on mathematical problems, and quantum algorithms can solve those problems. Bitcoin developers are discussing migration to more secure algorithms, but Ethereum’s 2029 deflation goal may be forced to be delayed due to migration costs.

Impact on the market
In the short term, this news will strengthen institutional demand for BTC/ETH as a "digital gold" hedge. With Bitcoin currently at about $83K and Ethereum at about $2,650, their value lies not only in their transaction functions, but also in their security characteristics that are difficult to replicate. If quantum threats intensify, they may drive:
1. Accelerated capital inflows into the crypto market’s "security arbitrage" flows
2. Regulators forcing institutional investors to allocate to quantum-resistant encrypted assets
3. Ethereum developers’ migration roadmap possibly becoming more aggressive than expected

Historically, similar discussions included the 2017 talk of "SHA-256 under quantum computing attack," when the market reaction was muted. But this year, regulators issued an official warning for the first time, meaning awareness of the threat has shifted from academia to the regulatory sphere.

💡 This news means crypto’s "security margin" is being reassessed. If quantum computing achieves breakthrough progress in the next 1–2 years, this judgment will be invalid. With Bitcoin at about $83K and Ethereum at about $2,650, their prices currently include roughly a 5% quantum risk premium. If developers can complete the post-quantum migration before 2025, this premium would disappear.

📰 Why BlackRock’s Collaboration Can Change Digital Asset Custody?

Ondo Network announced a partnership with BlackRock, the world’s largest asset management firm, to develop tokenized smart investment portfolios. This is a big deal for the crypto community, because it means traditional financial giants are finally taking blockchain-based wealth management seriously. In the future, everyday people may not need to buy mutual funds; they can turn their money into tokens and place them on the Ondo platform to enjoy investment strategies similar to those used by BlackRock—liquidity, transparency, and flexibility are all significantly improved. This is an important signal for the development of on-chain finance as a whole.

Why is this news important?
The core reason is that digital asset custody has been far too unreliable—most DeFi platforms carry a high risk of rug pulls, while traditional financial institutions are still clinging to old methods. The Ondo + BlackRock partnership implies: 1) BlackRock recognizes blockchain’s potential as an investment tool; and 2) tokenized assets can finally connect seamlessly with the traditional financial system. This is completely the opposite of the earlier situation where Buffett famously came out against Bitcoin—top-tier institutions are now stepping in personally to play with digital assets.

Market impact
In the short term, BTC and ETH may see a sentiment rebound thanks to this news. After all, BlackRock’s move is essentially “backed by facts,” directly giving the market a reassurance. In the medium to long term, tokenized assets will bring more mainstream capital into crypto, especially benefiting major coins like BTC. A historical reference is the period around the introduction of ETFs in 2021—capital inflow curves were almost perfectly overlapping. This time the pattern is similar, but goes even deeper.

Trading outlook
💡 In this leg of the market, if BTC can hold steady at the key level of $82,000, it may be able to kick off a new round of upside. But if regulators suddenly flip their stance or BlackRock changes its mind, this view becomes invalid. Why? Because the compliance of tokenized assets remains the biggest uncertainty.

Ondo Network 宣布和全球最大的资产管理公司 BlackRock 合作开发代币化智能投资组合。这对币圈来说是大事，因为这意味着传统金融巨头开始认真对待用区块链技术做财富管理了。普通人以后可能不用买基金，直接把钱变成代币放 Ondo 平台上，就能享受类似黑石的投资策略，流动性、透明度和灵活性都大大提高。这对整个链上金融发展是重要信号。

为什么这条新闻重要？
根本原因是数字资产托管太不靠谱了——大部分 DeFi 平台跑路风险高，而传统金融机构又死抱着旧方法不放。Ondo + BlackRock 的合作意味着：1）黑石认可了区块链作为投资工具的潜力；2）代币化资产终于能和传统金融体系无缝对接了。这跟之前巴菲特唱空比特币完全相反，顶级机构正在亲自下场玩数字资产。

After leverage declines, whether spot buying can pick up the market.

U.S. 10-year Treasury yields have risen to levels near the highest since 2007; the U.S. dollar is strengthening, putting simultaneous pressure on stocks and the crypto market.
